title: Dental PPO Plans Waiting-Period Credit on the Requested Payment of Claim Appeals
content:
**Appeal credit.** On a second-level post-service appeal of the Dental PPO Plans under the claim-appeal rule, the months the requested payment credits toward its waiting period follow the person's earlier coverage, and so decide the amount in dispute:
- when the plan credits prior coverage month for month and the person (matched by name and date of birth) has a terminated Cascade enrollment in the Prepaid Dental HMO Plans that ended on the day before the Dental PPO enrollment's coverage effective date (a move from the DHMO with no break in coverage), the appeal credit is the calendar months from the month that DHMO coverage took effect through the month it ended, both months counted (DHMO coverage always takes effect on the first of a month);
- when the plan credits prior coverage month for month, no such DHMO enrollment exists, and the enrollment shows documented prior coverage months whose prior coverage end date is no more than 63 calendar days before the coverage effective date, the appeal credit is those documented months;
- otherwise no months are credited.

The months credited shorten the waiting period, never below zero.

**By plan.** Month for month on Value 1000, Classic 1250, Plus 1500, Premier 2000 and Elite 2500; none on Preventive 750; 63 calendar days on every plan.

**Example (hypothetical).** A late entrant whose DHMO coverage ran 1 January to 30 November, with Dental PPO coverage effective 1 December and a plan change on 1 July of the next year to a plan with a 12-month major late-entrant waiting period: 11 months are credited, 1 month remains, and a major line dated 1 August counts as past the waiting period.
